sweep_summary: One sweep item for Ao Naga (aona1235, catalog: no-word-stress on Coupe 2003): Temsunungsang 2009, the EFLU Hyderabad PhD thesis on Ao prosodic phonology. Abstract, contents and chapters 1, 2 and 5 were already on file from the 2026-09-16 audit; I extracted the chapter 1-2 text and read the stress passages. Chapter 5 (pp. 118, 130, 147) states outright that Ao lacks a stress system (no evidence from intensity, duration or pitch; tone not attracted to any position) and builds foot structure from tone and minimality instead; chapter 2 adds that vowel reduction is consonant-conditioned, not stress-conditioned. This CONFIRMS the catalog coding as an independent native-speaker source; it does not supersede Coupe 2003, whose acoustic measurements remain the deciding record. Attempts to fetch the remaining chapters (3, 4, 6, bibliography) failed: Shodhganga timed out on all hosts today (low priority, chapter 5 is the stress chapter). Two other held Ao sources re-checked: Temsunungsang & Changkija 2025 (Changki-Ao phonology) has no stress statement; Walling 2017 ch. 3 mentions stress only in general remarks about tone languages.1017/upo9788175968431.005, not a stress title). written at

new_statements.quote: The structure of the foot and its rhythmic pattern is one aspect of Ao phonology which has been neglected in previous research studies (Gowda 1975, Coupe 2003, 2007; Temsunungsang 2006). This is perhaps due to the lack of evidence with respect to stress; intensity, duration and pitch. Unlike other tonal languages (de Lacy 1999, 2002), tones in Ao do not show any evidence of stress being attracted to certain positions in a word. [...] This is mainly because of the lack of a stress system in the language, and the question arises as to whether a metrical foot is/can be built at all.
new_statements.citation: Temsunungsang, T. 2009. Aspects of the prosodic phonology of Ao: An inter-dialectal study. PhD thesis, The English and Foreign Languages University, Hyderabad. hdl.handle.net/10603/108955
new_statements.reading: Ao (Chungli and Mongsen) has no word-stress system: no acoustic correlate (intensity, duration, pitch) marks a fixed prominent syllable and tone is not attracted to any position; prosodic structure is carried by tone and syllable-count minimality. Independent second confirmation of the catalog's no-word-stress coding.

sources.note: First-hand phonological study of Chungli and Mongsen Ao by a native-speaker linguist. States repeatedly that Ao has no stress system: no evidence for stress from intensity, duration or pitch, and tones show no attraction to any word position. Foot structure is argued for on other grounds (disyllabic minimality, vowel augmentation, schwa deletion, binary tone spreading); the author proposes a violable right-aligned trochaic foot and a tonal foot built from de Lacy's tonal prominence hierarchy (H most prominent), explicitly 'without reference to traditional stress related' factors.
